scope: Current-render target grounding, required part coverage, explicit model selection, prohibited-model request guards, provider payload compatibility and retained project lifecycle

backend.kind: Actual Python modules, Flask test clients and temporary SQLite/file projects; external AI, Blender and transport mocked at tested boundaries

frontend.kind: Actual app HTML and JavaScript with mocked APIs

static_checks.kind: HTML references, ARIA reference integrity, JavaScript syntax and CSS parsing; no pixel/browser accessibility audit
static_checks.preservationExampleInPlaceholder: 例如：反光柔和一点，颜色和角度不变

offline_preview.kind: Generated offline pages: jsdom DOM/state checks and JS/CSS parsing; no browser visual verification

limitations: Both revisions and five iframe dimensions were exercised. jsdom does not verify responsive pixel layout, clipping or visual appearance.

The upload is a local FormData demonstration and the background progression uses labelled fixture timers. No real files were uploaded to a server, no external AI was invoked, and Blender was not executed.

notes: The prohibited model is checked before image payload construction and again before network transport; no automatic paid model switch is added.
Reference prices come from official documentation and include date/region/tier notes; they are not a quote for any existing gateway account.
Visible ray samples establish object/material identity at those pixels; semantic classification and hidden part completeness are not empirically benchmarked.
Part coverage tests prevent explicit quantity, shared-material or missing-target requests from silently becoming partial edits.
Source .env bytes are preserved in the source archive and excluded from the cumulative patch; the regression harness never reads the actual configuration.
The two historical missing-fixture errors are not counted as passes.
Offline preview interactions and images are explicitly simulated; jsdom dimensions are not browser pixel acceptance.
